home.latest-news.the-holy-see-says-pope-: Pope Leo XIV was discharged from Gemelli Hospital on Saturday afternoon following lung surgery and returned to the Vatican. On Sunday he prayed the midday Angelus with thousands of faithful gathered in St Peter's Square - his first scheduled public event since being discharged - thanking the doctors, nurses and staff of Gemelli and all who prayed for him: 'I have truly felt your support.' On Wednesday, October 21, he held his first weekly General Audience since the surgery in St Peter's Square, Vatican News reported; he thanked people for their prayers and spoke on marriage and the family in his catechesis on Gaudium et Spes. RTE and ANSA also reported on the audience. Context photo: Gemelli Hospital, Rome. Photo: Blackcat, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0 IT; resized to WebP.
home.saintDay.2026-10-21.heading: Saint of the Day
home.saintDay.2026-10-21.name: Saint Hilarion
home.saintDay.2026-10-21.story: Hilarion was born in Palestine to a pagan family and studied in Alexandria, where he became a Christian. Through Saint Anthony the Abbot he learned to love contemplative solitude, prayer and penance. He withdrew as a hermit to Maiumma, where he founded several monasteries and brought about conversions. He died in Paphos.

home.saintDay.2026-10-22.heading: Saint of the Day
home.saintDay.2026-10-22.name: Saint John Paul II
home.saintDay.2026-10-22.story: Karol Wojtyła, born in 1920 in Wadowice, Poland, lost his mother at nine and his brother at twelve. During the German occupation he worked in a stone quarry and a chemical plant, then was ordained a priest in 1946. Elected pope in 1978, he cried out at his inaugural Mass on October 22: “Do not be afraid! Open wide the doors to Christ!” He died on April 2, 2005, was beatified in 2011 and declared a saint in 2014.

home.saintDay.2026-10-23.name: Saint Ignatius of Constantinople
home.saintDay.2026-10-23.story: Ignatius, born Nicetas about 799, was the son of Emperor Michael I. After his father was deposed he was shut in a monastery, where he embraced the religious life and became an abbot. In 847 he became Patriarch of Constantinople. He refused to help force the empress Theodora into a convent and rebuked the Caesar Bardas for repudiating his wife, and Bardas had him sent into exile. Restored in 867, he served about ten more years and died on October 23, 877.
